title: Fast Hubbard-Thouless Pumping with Local Counterdiabatic Driving
abstract: Counterdiabatic (CD) driving suppresses the excitations of fast protocols by adding an auxiliary Hamiltonian, but in many-body and topological systems the exact CD term is generally non-local and multi-body. We study this obstruction for Thouless pumping in the Rice-Mele model, first without and then with interactions. For noninteracting fermions, the exact CD term of the pump is non-local, but the variational framework of Sels and Polkovnikov yields accurate nearest-neighbor approximations. For the spinful Rice-Mele chain with onsite and nearest-neighbor repulsion, in the regime where the competition of the two interactions stabilizes quantized pumping, this approach fails: the infinite-temperature variational action only penalizes the CD amplitudes, and the resulting two-parameter nearest-neighbor term does not prevent the pump from breaking down when the cycle time is reduced from $50/t$ to $2/t$. We trace the failure to the structure of the exact many-body gauge potential, whose amplitude for each hop depends on the interaction energy that the hop costs. Resolving the nearest-neighbor currents by this energy, and fixing the coefficients with a ground-state-weighted action, gives a local ansatz with 14 coefficients that keeps the interacting pump quantized for cycle times $T=2/t$ and $T=1/t$, with an accuracy per site that does not degrade between rings of 8 and 12 sites.
summary: This paper tackles the difficulty of implementing fast quantum control in interacting many-body systems by analyzing the required counterdiabatic driving Hamiltonian. The authors show that standard variational methods fail when interactions are present, proposing a novel, interaction-resolved local ansatz that successfully quantizes the topological pumping even at very fast driving speeds.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving fast, transitionless quantum evolution (Thouless pumping) in interacting many-body systems where the exact counterdiabatic (CD) driving term is non-local and multi-body.
main_result: By developing an interaction-resolved local ansatz with 14 coefficients, the authors successfully maintained quantized pumping for fast cycle times in the interacting Rice-Mele model, overcoming the failure of standard variational approximations.
method: The study combines the theory of Counterdiabatic driving with variational principles applied to the action functional, specifically resolving the gauge potential dependence on interaction energy.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Rice-Mele chain, extended to include onsite and nearest-neighbor Hubbard-type interactions. The analysis also draws parallels with the Kitaev chain and general many-body gauge potentials.
key_observables: Quantized pumped charge (topological pumping), the stability of the pumping mechanism under fast driving, and the structure of the many-body gauge potential.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths (U, V), hopping parameters (t, $\Delta$), and the cycle time $T$ (e.g., $T=2/t$ and $T=1/t$).
main_assumptions: The standard variational approach fails for interacting systems; the solution relies on constructing a local ansatz whose coefficients are determined by a ground-state-weighted action that explicitly accounts for interaction energy costs.
figures_summary: Figure 10 shows the fitted intracell coefficients for the $\Delta E$-resolved ansatz, demonstrating how these coefficients change as a function of the local interaction energy $\epsilon$.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the general theory of CD driving and its application to topological systems (Kitaev chain). It then focuses on the Thouless pumping in the Rice-Mele model, contrasting the noninteracting case with the interacting case, culminating in the proposal and validation of the 14-coefficient local ansatz.
why_interesting: The work provides a sophisticated theoretical framework for controlling quantum dynamics in strongly correlated materials, moving beyond simple non-interacting approximations by incorporating interaction-dependent gauge potentials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Time evolution of the population of state 1 in a spin-1/2 system with energy gap ω0 = 10. a) Breakdown of the adiabatic approximation when driving fast using only the reference Hamiltonian H0. b) Perfect tracking of the adiabatic path recovered by adding the CD term H1.

Figure 1 confirms that this simple example already cap- tures the essential feature of CD driving: with only H0, the adiabatic approximation for the state populations vis- ibly breaks down at fast rotation rates (large ˙θ), whereas adding H1 makes the exact and adiabatic solutions coin- cide for any ˙θ [19] – the system tracks the ground state exactly regardless of driving speed. Realizing H1 directly is generally difficult experimen- tally, since it demands access to the full non-local, multi- qubit operator content of the auxiliary term. An es- tablished alternative is to synthesize an equivalent ef- fective Hamiltonian using a fast periodic (Floquet) drive
